=== Summary ===
The founding era is unknown. Shrine tradition says that when {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto}} made his eastern campaign, he established a main sanctuary here, and later when {{ill|Kibi no Takehiko|Q18226257|qid=Q18226257}}, vice commander of that campaign, came to rule this area, he built shrine buildings at the former main sanctuary and enshrined Yamato Takeru. It was once also called "Kyūman-hassen-sha" (Ninety-eight-thousand Shrine), said to have enshrined 98,000 people who accompanied Yamato Takeru's eastern campaign, and at rites 98,000 {{ill|Hanpei|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885}} were dedicated.

The oldest record in documents appears in the '{{ill|Suruga no Kuni Fudoki|Q11668491|qid=Q11668491}}', saying official offerings were presented in year 1 of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|Q316672|qid=Q316672}} (133). In a variant text of the Ruijū Rikkokushi, it says that in year 1 of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} (859) it was granted Junior Second Rank in the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} divine rank system.

In the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}' it is listed as "Kusanagi Shrine, Ihara District, Suruga Province," ranked as small shrine. Since {{ill|Kusanagi Shrine|Q11618229|qid=Q11618229}} in Udo District (present Shimizu-ku Kusanagi), also a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, has the same name and also enshrines Yamato Takeru, this shrine was called "East Kusanagi Shrine" until the Edo period to distinguish them. In Meiji 6 it became a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}, returning to the original name Kusanagi Shrine.
